answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a single ordered admission gate: each new identity wins its slot by burning a bid, and every winning bid raises the floor price for the next slot, so a farm chasing a thousand fakes pays a climbing price a thousand separate times. The gate is a mesa, wide but flat and finite, while unbought identities drift in a nebula of zero weight. A farm that stops bidding falls to the nadir of the queue, behind every honest newcomer.
